name: Question 5
problem:
What is ${\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{x+1}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{x+1}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[$
{{field-1}}
$\cdot \frac{3}{n}]$
worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{x+1}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\sqrt{x+1},$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the upper bound is $b=3.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3-0}{n}=\frac{3}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(0+i\cdot \frac{3}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(\frac{3i}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[\sqrt{(\frac{3i}{n})+1}\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[\,\sqrt{\frac{3i}{n}+1}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑i=1nf(xi)⋅Δx,

where xi=a+iΔx and Δx=b−an.

In the definite integral

∫03x+1dx,

the function is f(x)=x+1, the lower bound is a=0 and the upper bound is b=3. So, we have

Δx=3−0n=3n.

Therefore,

∫03x+1dx=limn→∞∑i=1nf(xi)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑i=1n[f(0+i⋅3n)⋅3n]=limn→∞∑i=1n[f(3in)⋅3n]=limn→∞∑i=1n[(3in)+1⋅3n]=limn→∞∑i=1n[3in+1⋅3n].
